justification:
# DR-UI-03: the board chrome is DOM, not canvas (board-free)

No board fixture can show this difference: it is in the board UI around the canvas (tool bars,
popovers, menus, lists, labels, switches, panels, arrowhead previews, shape library cells), not in
anything a board draws. Any board shows it; the comparison uses the synthetic
`lekhcore/test/fixtures/boards/ipad-flowchart.lekh` on the offline board:

- `e2e/tests/board-screens-parity.spec.js` (AC-UI-18) with `SCREENS_CPP_URL` at the C++ web build
  and `E2E_BASE_URL` at the TS front end: every pair now differs by 0.1-1.1 % of its pixels (bar
  0.1 %), from 1 px frame borders the browser snaps to whole pixels (C++ spread them over two
  half-covered pixels) and labels about half a pixel lower (DOM text, not canvas `top` text);
- the TS board has 3 canvases on every screen (`document.querySelectorAll('canvas')`), where the
  canvas-drawn chrome had 12 on an idle desktop board and up to 105 with the shape library open.

Owner decision 2026-10-22 (Work 01M4X7TCHFB862XGT68GPY071C, round DOM1): best effort to match
the C++ look with React only, relaxed where it cannot match, because WebKit caps the canvas memory
of a web process.
